stemMd: Points $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a circle with center $O$ and radius $9$. Point $C$ lies on the major arc $AB$, and inscribed angle $ACB$ measures $70^\circ$. What is the length of minor arc $AB$?
explanationMd:
An inscribed angle measures **half** the central angle that intercepts the same arc. Inscribed angle $ACB$ intercepts minor arc $AB$, so the central angle $AOB$ is

$$2 \times 70^\circ = 140^\circ$$

Arc length is the fraction of the full circle that the central angle covers, times the circumference:

$$\text{arc } AB = \frac{140}{360} \times 2\pi(9) = \frac{7}{18} \times 18\pi = 7\pi$$

Check the complementary arc: the major arc is $\frac{220}{360} \times 18\pi = 11\pi$, and $7\pi + 11\pi = 18\pi$, the whole circumference.

The trap is treating the $70^\circ$ inscribed angle as if it were the central angle, which gives half the correct length.

distractorRationale.b: This uses the inscribed angle, $70^\circ$, as the central angle: $\frac{70}{360} \times 18\pi = \frac{7\pi}{2}$. The central angle is twice the inscribed angle, $140^\circ$.
distractorRationale.c: This is the length of the major arc, $\frac{220}{360} \times 18\pi = 11\pi$. The question asks for the minor arc, which the $140^\circ$ central angle intercepts.
distractorRationale.d: This uses the diameter, $18$, as the radius, doubling the circumference to $36\pi$ and giving $\frac{140}{360} \times 36\pi = 14\pi$.

accessibilityText: Points A, B and C lie on a circle with center O and radius 9. C is on the major arc AB, and inscribed angle ACB measures 70 degrees. What is the length of minor arc AB? The choices are 7 pi, 7 pi over 2, 11 pi, and 14 pi.

provenance.notes: Original item. Combines the inscribed angle theorem with arc length; distractors come from using the inscribed angle as central, finding the major arc, and using the diameter as the radius.
